title: rwb-reporting steering dashboard (application slice): the consumed operation names, the workflow and activity names, the read-model design, the INT-19 replacement and the agent fact source are fixed by no single source
source: Work Package B2-P9-002 story line (service rwb-reporting, patterns DP01, DP03, DP07, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP17, DP19); Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.4, R5.5, R5.7 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 16; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A1.2, A2.3 and A2.8; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T5.1, T5.2 and Appendix T-A; P9 context pack (ownership rows, connection matrix)
description: One combined row for the application slice of RWB-E2-009. (1) Consumption: the legacy story calls six Java interfaces — CaseReportingApi.caseFacts, CaseReportingApi.openCaseCount, DecisionLogApi.decisionFacts, TreatmentApi.treatmentFacts, NoticeApi.noticeFacts and AgentMonitorApi.runFacts — and no published document fixes the target operation names, paths, payloads or errors of the case facts, the agent runs or the freshness check. (2) Scheduling and naming: JOB-15 is a Quartz and Spring Batch job in the sources and a Temporal Schedule under DP-10, and no source names the Schedule, the workflow or its activities; the story names them as a design choice. (3) Read model: the context pack gives the service three tables only, so no fact table can be added for the event-derived read model; the story replays the day's events into a run-scoped view, and no source fixes that mechanism. (4) INT-19: AC1 asserts an INT-19 extract in a data lake, Arch v5 removes the data lake and INT-19 under DP-17, and no source says how the 07:30 Power BI refresh reaches the published rows in the target; the story hands the extract to rwb-integration and keeps the freshness stamp. (5) Agent facts: the legacy AgentMonitorApi is P10's, the connection matrix shows no REST or event row from P10 to P9, and the plan scopes the agent facts as RWB-P10-E1063-CON only; the story reads both EV-28 and that contract. (6) Migration: the legacy migration V2_009__measure_publish.sql is the monolith's, and the parent slice RWB-P9-E1013-APP already creates the three tables. (7) Coverage: the Work Package assigns all nine criteria to this slice and none of the key is left unowned.
evidence: RWB-E2-009 section 12 lists the six Java interfaces and the two operation rows, section 13 names the migration V2_009__measure_publish.sql and the new table measure_publish, and section 4 step 4 writes the 'INT-19 extract with the freshness stamp'; FSD P9 v3 A2.3 and A2.8 give AC-P9-003-01 and AC-P9-008-01 with the INT-19 extract; TSD P9 v2 T5.1 names INT-19 as 'Data lake and Power BI, Out, Daily batch', T3.1 carries three tables only and Appendix T-A one operation; the P9 context pack gives one REST operation, three tables, one job JOB-15, no event and no workflow, and the connection matrix row of P9 shows events from P3, S2, S3, S6, S7 and P6 and Temporal calls to P1 and P2 only.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-agent, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration and the reporting service
proposed: Declare the three consumed operations and the two owner-queue activities on the per-service bases and queues with one hop and a 2 s timeout, take the element names from the owners at review, replay the day's events into a run-scoped read model instead of adding a fact table, hand the published day's extract to rwb-integration as the INT-19 replacement, take the agent rates from EV-28 and RWB-P10-E1063-CON, and keep the three parent tables as RWB-P9-E1013-CON fixes them.

title: rwb-reporting steering dashboard (contract slice): the element names of the consumed declarations, the event envelope naming, the Measure delta, the schema increments and the file shape of the extract are fixed by no single source
source: Work Package B2-P9-002 story line (work type CON, patterns all nine); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5, R7.2 s12, R8.2 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 12 and 13; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T5.1, T5.3 and Appendix T-A; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.3.3.2 and A2.8.4; P9 context pack ownership rows
description: One combined row for the contract slice. (1) The legacy story gives Java interfaces, so the request and response element names of the case-list, agent-run and reference-data declarations and of the two owner-queue activities are a review baseline and carry the placeholder where no published document fixes them. (2) Event envelopes: the Event and Messaging Design v4 gives payload lists and consumer names but no envelope elements, subject or schema-registry naming per subscription. (3) The Measure delta: RWB-E2-009 section 12 asks for dimension and baselineValue while the API Specification carries neither, and no column carries a baseline value, so the field is derived from the frozen baseline rows rather than added to measure_snapshot. (4) The schema increments: the parent tag RWB-P9-E1013-CON already carries the three tables and their field sets, so the uniqueness of business_date and the two indexes are the only schema objects this key can add; no source names them. (5) The service's ownership row carries no event, so the topic rwb.reporting.events.v1 carries no schema of this key; no source states that either. (6) The extract that replaces INT-19 has no documented file shape or trailer in the target. (7) Status is Draft (realignment v1) and the baseline is published without an approval.
evidence: RWB-E2-009 section 12 gives the request, the response, the errors and the note that the Measure schema has no dimension or baseline field, and section 13 names the table measure_publish and the index on measure_snapshot (measure_code, business_date, product_group); TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-A gives API-P9-001 with its request, response and errors, T3.1 gives DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-058, T3.2 the five lists and T5.3 'Events: None'; the P9 context pack gives one operation, three tables, no event, jobs JOB-15 and no workflow; RWB-P9-E1013-CON already declares the same operation and the same three tables.
owner_role: Contract owner of rwb-reporting, with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-agent, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration and the event platform
proposed: Publish version v1 as an increment on the parent tag: the baselineValue delta, the fixing of dimension, the three declarations, the two activity contracts, the eight subscriptions with their groups, the registration contract of JOB-15, the message map and a fake per declaration; mark every unsettled element with the placeholder and one review row; gate the tag on the contract tests and the schema lint.

title: rwb-reporting steering dashboard (deployment slice): the login and secret reference, the replica and threshold values, the consumer offset and retention policy, the catch-up window, the backfill limit and the message ID of the run alert are fixed by no source
source: Work Package B2-P9-002 story line (work type OPS, lane L-P9-C, owner DEVOPS); Template and Rules v1 R4, R5.5, R5.7 and R9; legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 5, 10, 13 and 14; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.3.4.3 and A2.8.4.3; TSD P9 Reporting v2 Appendix T-B; P9 context pack (schema, base, topic, queue, namespace)
description: One combined row for the deployment slice. (1) Identity: no source names the login secret reference, the connection pool size, the replica counts or the resource requests of rwb-reporting. (2) Consumers: no source fixes the partition count, the retention, the offset policy or the catch-up window of the eight consumer groups of the service, which consumes and publishes nothing of its own. (3) Observability: no source fixes the six alert thresholds, the aggregation window of the four series, their dimensions or the run window after which a missing execution is an alert. (4) Runbook: no source names the six runbook entries, their owner roles or their review cycle. (5) Run controls: no source fixes the backfill limit per run, the build ID format, the worker versioning policy or the Schedule time zone. (6) Messages: the flag-off and run-not-started paths carry no legacy business message and no message ID is allocated for them. (7) Approval: the story carries no approval and the first environment is non-production. (8) The legacy story fixes no deployment value and names no identity; it assumed a shared recovery login, a Quartz trigger and a shared job monitor.
evidence: RWB-E2-009 section 13 names the feature flag rwb.reporting.steering, a folder and a package and no deployment value; section 10 names roles and no login or secret reference; section 14 gives four message IDs with no routing; TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-B leaves DL06, DL11 and DL35 open, and DL11 is the non-functional target values; the P9 context pack fixes the schema rwb_reporting, the base, the topic, the queue and the namespace and no deployment value; the FSD P9 v3 A1.4 states only that a data product carries today's business date or shows its date as stale.
owner_role: DevOps team, with the platform administrator, the observability owner, the event platform owner and the workflow kit owner
proposed: Ship one chart with an api and a worker deployment, a migration increment, the Schedule, the eight consumer groups, six alerts with their runbook links, four dashboard series, the flag, the backfill and the rollback; take every threshold, count, offset and limit as a value of the environment; allocate the missing run message ID with the catalogue owner; and review the six runbook entries with the on-call rota before promotion.
